question.text: For the reaction <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mn>6</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>5</mn></msub><mo>.</mo><msub><mi>NH</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><munderover><mo>→</mo><mrow><mn>180</mn><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi>SO</mi><mn>4</mn></msub></mrow></munderover><munder><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo>·</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mn>6</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><mfenced><mrow><msub><mi>SO</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow></mfenced></mrow><mfenced><mi>Para</mi></mfenced></munder></math> the true statement about the product is

options.text: it does not exist as Zwitter ion
it does not act as inner salt

solution.text:
A zwitterion is a compound with no overall electrical charge, but which contains separate parts which are positively and negatively charged.

Sulphanilic acid exist as dipolar ion (zwitter ion); act as inner salt and SO3H group diminishes the basic character of -NH2.
